name: Core words
description: Single words you can point with. Nouns, adjectives, question words, and a few verbs.

cards.tip: Noun. The o- prefix makes it polite in requests: omizu. Cold water by default; hot water is oyu.
The o- is baked in; nobody says cha alone. Green tea unless specified; koucha is black tea.
Loanword in katakana. Long o and long i: koo-hii. aisu koohii = iced coffee.
Loanword. nama biiru = draft beer. Long i.
go- is an honorific prefix fused to han (cooked rice). Also means a meal: asagohan is breakfast.
Noun. gyuuniku (beef), butaniku (pork), toriniku (chicken) all end in niku.
Fish, both the animal and the food. Japanese nouns have no plural.
Vegetables. No plural marking; yasai covers one or many.
Train station. Name + eki: Shinjuku eki. Bus terminals are not eki.
den (electric) + sha (vehicle). The subway is chikatetsu; shinkansen is its own word.
Loanword in katakana. Also 'bath'; context decides.
Loanword. Taxi doors open automatically; the driver does it.
Loanword. A ryokan is a traditional inn, a different word.
Clipped from 'convenience store'. Japanese shortens long loanwords freely.
From 'toilet'. otearai (o- + te + arai, hand washing) is the politer word on signs.
o- + kane (metal, money). The o- is nearly always kept on this word.
Loanword. kurejitto kaado in full; kaado alone is understood.
gen (present) + kin (money). genkin de = in cash.
A bag or sack. A handbag or backpack is kaban or baggu.
I, me. Neutral and safe in any setting. Men casually use boku or ore. Dropped when obvious from context.
Friend or friends. tomodachi to = with friends.
What. Becomes nan before desu, to, no: nan desu ka. nani o = what (as an object).
Where. The do- member of the koko, soko, asoko set.
When. Takes no particle: itsu ikimasu ka.
Who. Polite: donata.
How much, for price. ikutsu is how many, or how old.
This thing, near me. kore o kudasai works for anything you can point at.
That thing, near you. sore wa nan desu ka.
That thing over there, far from both of you. Said ah-reh, not like English 'are'.
i-adjective with a long o. Before a noun: ookii kaban. Opposite: chiisai.
i-adjective with a long i. chiisakunai = not small.
Hot: weather and temperature. atsui also means thick, with a different kanji.
Cold weather, or feeling cold. Cold to the touch is tsumetai.
Good. Irregular: past and negative use yo-: yokatta (was good), yokunai (not good).
Bad. kibun ga warui = feel sick. warui ne is a casual 'my bad'.
na-adjective, so 'I like X' is X ga suki desu, with ga. daisuki = love it.
A little. Also the universal softener: chotto... on its own means 'that's a bit (difficult)', a polite no.
More. motto yukkuri = more slowly. Compare mou (again, another).
Polite present of iku (go). Also the future: Japanese has no separate future tense. Past: ikimashita.
Polite form of taberu. The -masu ending is the polite present/future on every verb. Past: tabemashita. Negative: tabemasen.
Polite form of nomu (drink). Also used for taking medicine: kusuri o nomimasu.
Polite form of kau (buy). kaimono = shopping, the noun.
Polite form of miru: see, look, watch. mite kudasai = please look.
Existence or possession for things. Negative: arimasen. For people and animals use imasu.
Please give me. After a noun (+ o) it asks for a thing; after a -te form it asks for an action.
desu (is, polite) + ka (question). Noun + desu ka asks 'is it X?'. No rising intonation needed; ka does the work.
